title: Performance envelope and capacity validation plan
workflow: Collect institutional branch/channel/batch and seasonality assumptions
Define separately steady, peak, stress, saturation and recovery scenarios
Generate approved anonymized workload fixtures with realistic account and event distribution
Measure request p50/p95/p99, queue lag, posting conservation and report consistency
Repeat under database failure, broker replay and delayed external network conditions
Publish hardware profile, reproducible results, bottlenecks and acceptance decisions
requirements: Do not infer capacity from a marketing target or an unexecuted synthetic benchmark
Correctness and end-of-day reconciliation outrank higher nominal TPS
Record external dependency constraints separately from internal application performance
Measure tenant isolation and authorization cost under concurrent workloads
Performance tests must ensure zero duplicate or unbalanced journal postings
Stress tests must preserve complete audit and traceability while redacting sensitive data
tests: Run peak posting workload and compare journal debits/credits
Measure read projection staleness during high event volume
Introduce broker lag and verify recovery without duplicate commands
Test per-institution resource limits under multitenant load
Benchmark restore and reconciliation before allowing production resume
gate: Signed workload assumptions, available benchmark environment, executed load/fault tests and independent Operations/CFO result review.
